vulnerability.title: Add noexec Option to /dev/shm
vulnerability.description: The noexec mount option can be used to prevent binaries from being executed out of /dev/shm. It can be dangerous to allow the execution of binaries from world-writable temporary storage directories such as /dev/shm. Add the noexec option to the fourth column of /etc/fstab for the line which controls mounting of /dev/shm.
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if ( ! ( { rpm --quiet -q kernel-core ;} && { rpm --quiet -q rpm-ostree ;} && { rpm --quiet -q bootc ;} && { ! rpm --quiet -q openshift-kubelet ;} && ([ -f /run/ostree-booted ] || [ -L /ostree ]) ) && ! ( [ -f /.dockerenv ] || [ -f /run/.containerenv ] ) ); then function perform_remediation { mount_point_match_regexp="$(printf "^[[:space:]]*[^#].*[[:space:]]%s[[:space:]]" /dev/shm)" # If the mount point is not in /etc/fstab, get previous mount options from /etc/mtab if ! grep -q "$mount_point_match_regexp" /etc/fstab; then # runtime opts without some automatic kernel/userspace-added defaults previous_mount_opts=$(grep "$mount_point_match_regexp" /etc/mtab | head -1 | awk '{print $4}' \ | sed -E "s/(rw|defaults|seclabel|noexec)(,|$)//g;s

triage_decision.reason: Adding the noexec option to /dev/shm is a standard hardening practice that prevents execution of binaries from a world-writable temporary directory. It does not affect authentication, networking, or critical services, and can be applied safely without system lockout.
triage_decision.estimated_impact: filesystems affected; Potential failure of applications that rely on executing binaries from /dev/shm

previous_review_verdicts.feedback: The plan correctly restores the original /etc/fstab, updates the /dev/shm entry to include noexec (and nodev) options, remounts the filesystem, and verifies the change. This will effectively remediate the vulnerability. The approach is safe, preserves other fstab contents, and uses standard tools. It could be streamlined by appending noexec to existing options rather than replacing the whole line, but the current method still achieves the desired outcome.
concerns: The sed replacement overwrites the entire /dev/shm line, which may remove other legitimate options such as nosuid or defaults that were present in the original fstab.
The remount operation assumes no other dependent services will be impacted; if /dev/shm is heavily used, a brief service interruption may occur.
The backup restore step relies on the existence of a backup; if it is missing, the script may fail or revert to an incorrect state.
suggested_improvements:
Modify the sed command to append 'noexec' (and optionally 'nodev') to the existing options column, preserving any other options the administrator had configured.
Use a strict pattern match (e.g., '^\s*/dev/shm\b') to avoid accidental edits of similar lines.
Add error handling to confirm both the fstab write and remount succeeded before exiting.
Optional: use 'systemctl daemon-reload' or other mechanisms if the scrip might be applied to systems with automatic fstab reloading.
Consider adding a check to ensure mountpoint is currently present and that the remount succeeds.
Back up to a specific, clearly named file rather than an autogenerated *.bak_... to avoid confusion.
Document the change in system change logs for audit purposes.
